tiles.text: From the 1870s, Métis homesteaders built a life on this land — farms, families, a church at its heart.

tiles.caption: The land remembers

tiles.text: 1935–1938. The PFRA forced the community out. Families scattered; the church was burned.
1938. Joe Venne refused to let the church be dismantled and saved it from destruction.
Decades later, only the foundations and the cemetery remain — and the memory held by descendants.
